title: Cancellation at the Named Insured's Request — RentGuard Renters Policy Return Premium
content:
## Who may cancel, and on what

- The named insured of a RentGuard Renters Policy cancels by a request recorded by the agent and signed by the named insured. A co-insured roommate cannot cancel the policy.
- The cancellation is processed only on a request the named insured has signed, as shown by the signature request on record for the policy.

## Cancellation date

- The cancellation date is not earlier than the date the signed request is received, unless it is backdated to a documented move-out date.
- A cancellation is backdated only to a move-out date shown on a lease termination or on a new residence's move-in document, by no more than the tier's backdating limit in days before the date the signed request is received, and only when no claim on the policy has a loss date on or after that move-out date. The move-out date comes from the customer's documents; the date the request was received and the loss dates of claims come from the company's records.

**Boundary cases (hypothetical; signed request received 20 May, backdating limit 30 days).** A move-out date of 20 April, 30 days earlier, may be used; 19 April may not. A claim on the policy with a loss date of 25 April blocks backdating to 20 April; a claim with a loss date of 18 April does not. On a tier whose backdating limit is 0, the cancellation is never dated before the day the signed request is received.

## Return premium

1. A cancellation on or before the effective date of a bound policy is flat: the whole term premium is credited, on a flat basis.
2. Otherwise the pro-rata unearned premium is the term premium — the annual premium at the current rating — multiplied by the calendar days from the cancellation date to the expiration date and divided by the calendar days in the term, rounded half-up to the cent.
3. On a tier returning pro rata, the whole unearned premium is returnable, on a pro-rata basis. On a tier returning short rate, the company keeps the tier's short-rate retention percentage of it and the rest is returnable, on a short-rate basis.
4. The cancellation credit is the returnable amount less the term's scheduled installments not yet billed, because unbilled installments are simply never billed.
5. The credit is then reduced, if needed, so that the premium kept for the term — everything billed for the term less the credit — is at least the tier's minimum earned premium.
6. When the credit works out below 0.00, no credit is posted and the difference is billed as one additional premium entry with change reason cancellation, dated the cancellation date.
7. A positive credit is posted as one return premium entry with change reason cancellation, dated the cancellation date, and the interested party, when one is listed, is notified.

The return basis, short-rate retention, minimum earned premium and backdating limit are the figures of the policy's own tier.

## Calculation sheet (hypothetical policies, 365-day terms)

**A — pro rata, monthly plan.** Term premium 240.00; cancellation 184 days before expiration. Unearned premium: 240.00 multiplied by 184, divided by 365, is 120.9863, rounded 120.99. Five installments of 20.00, 100.00 in all, are not yet billed: credit 20.99. Premium kept: 140.00 billed less 20.99 is 119.01, above a minimum earned premium of 50.00, so 20.99 is credited.

**B — short rate, annual plan.** Term premium 365.00; cancellation 120 days before expiration. Unearned premium 120.00; retention 10 percent keeps 12.00; returnable 108.00; nothing unbilled; premium kept 257.00; credit 108.00.

**C — credit below zero.** As B, but on a monthly plan with 150.00 of installments not yet billed: 108.00 less 150.00 is 42.00 below zero. No credit is posted; 42.00 is billed as additional premium dated the cancellation date.

**D — minimum earned premium.** Pro rata, annual plan, term premium 130.00, cancellation 355 days before expiration: unearned 126.44. Premium kept would be 3.56, below a minimum earned premium of 50.00, so the credit is reduced to 80.00, leaving 50.00 kept.
